Pumping Mode - Power Failure - Although not expected to occur, loss of power would cause a near instantaneous shut-down of the units. The draft tubes and tailrace tunnels would be designed to prevent structural damage due to such instantaneous shutdowns. A hydraulic system would be used to close the wicket gates to prevent backflow. This was considered as a possible operating incident and was taken into consideration in the design of the plant.
Pumping Mode - Failure to Stop Pumps After the Upper Reservoir Reaches Full Pond - Probability of occurrence is very remote. If the pumps were not shut down manually, power to the plant would be cut off automatically. A complete explanation of this automatic cutoff system in given in Subsection 1.4.2.2 of Exhibit W to the application.
Fire in the Powerhouse - Probability of occurrence is very remote. However, fire protection systems would be provided. Two exits from the powerhouse complex would be provided, the main access tunnel and the electric bus shaft. Carbon dioxide under pressure would be used for fire protection in the main generators. Normal station fire fighting equipment (hydrants and hoses) would be located throughout the underground complex.
Powerhouse Flooding - Probability of occurrence is very remote. Egress could be negotiated by the one access tunnel and the electrical bus shaft. The entire underground powerhouse complex would be drained to a central collection sump. This sump would be sized after an exploratory tunnel has been drilled and the leakage rate into the underground complex determined.
A schedule of maintenance and resulting outage time is shown in Table 4.1. The outage times do not include dewatering time. Necessary outages would be scheduled to cause minimum strain on the production systems. All maintenance work would be done to cause the least adverse environmental impact.
